common_core.title: The Source of Power
common_core.message: Priesthood authority comes by ordination, but priesthood power depends on your personal relationship with God. To have power, we must have a clean conduit to the Spirit.
common_core.challenge: Spend 5 minutes in total silence before your morning or evening prayer today. Focus on 'tuning' your heart to listen before you speak to God.

common_core.title: Your True Identity
common_core.message: You are not just a member of a church; you are part of a royal lineage. God has entrusted you with His divine authority. This identity should change how you walk and talk.
common_core.challenge: Look in the mirror today and say out loud: 'I am a son of God, and I hold His holy priesthood.' Act with that dignity all day.

common_core.title: The Power of Angels
common_core.message: The Aaronic Priesthood holds a spectacular promise: the ministering of angels. This means you have a right to angelic protection and guidance as you serve and remain worthy.
common_core.challenge: Pray specifically for the protection of one friend or family member who is struggling right now. Ask for the 'ministering of angels' to be with them.

common_core.title: Paying the Price
common_core.message: We cannot expect to have the power to bless others if we spend our time on 'spiritual junk food.' Increasing your power requires a sacrifice of time and focus.
common_core.challenge: Perform a 'Digital Audit.' Delete one app, unfollow one account, or skip one show today that lowers your spiritual sensitivity.

common_core.title: Where You Stand
common_core.message: A priesthood holder cannot be effective if he is constantly moving between the Lord's kingdom and the world's influence. You must decide where you stand and stay there.
common_core.challenge: Clean and organize your physical environment today (desk, room, or car). A clean space invites a clear mind and a holy spirit.

common_core.title: A Binding Promise
common_core.message: When you received the priesthood, you entered into a legal contract with God. You promise to magnify your calling, and He promises you everything He has.
common_core.challenge: Read D&C 84:33–44. Write down the specific things God promises to give you if you are faithful and keep them visible today.

common_core.title: The Weekly Reset
common_core.message: The Priesthood makes the Sacrament possible. This ordinance allows us to 'reset' our worthiness every week and keep the power of the Spirit flowing.
common_core.challenge: Tonight, write down one mistake from this week you want to 'leave at the sacrament table' tomorrow. Go to church with intent to be made new.

month_1.title: The Foundation of the Holy Priesthood
month_1.theme: The Work of Salvation and Exaltation

days.title: Living the Gospel
days.message: The first part of the work of salvation is living the gospel of Jesus Christ. Your priesthood power is a tool to help you grow in faith, repentance, and covenant keeping.
days.challenge: Choose one of the four responsibilities of the work of salvation and focus on it for the entire day.

days.title: Caring for Those in Need
days.message: Priesthood holders are called to mourn with those that mourn and comfort those that stand in need of comfort. This is the heart of your service.
days.challenge: Reach out to one person today—via text, call, or in person—whom you know is having a difficult time.

days.title: The Spirit of Invitation
days.message: Your joy will be great if you bring even one soul unto Christ. The priesthood is the authority used to gather Israel on both sides of the veil.
days.challenge: In your morning prayer, ask the Lord to put someone in your path today who needs a spiritual lift.

days.title: Uniting Families
days.message: There is a 'welding link' between generations. Priesthood ordinances in the temple bind families together forever.
days.challenge: Find one name of an ancestor on FamilySearch or ask a relative for a family story you didn't know.

days.title: Leading in the Home
days.message: By divine design, fathers are to preside over their families in love and righteousness. This is the primary place of priesthood service.
days.challenge: Do an anonymous chore or act of service for someone you live with (or a close family member).

days.title: Magnifying the Calling
days.message: To magnify a calling is to take it seriously, magnifying the Lord's power through your small efforts.
days.challenge: Study the specific duties of your office in the General Handbook for 10 minutes today.

days.title: Weekly Review
days.message: If you have felt to sing the song of redeeming love, can you feel so now? Spiritual momentum requires constant checking.
days.challenge: Journal for 5 minutes about the spiritual 'wins' you had this week and where you want to improve.

days.title: Authority vs. Power
days.message: Authority is the right to act; Power is the spiritual capacity to make that act effective. Power requires righteousness.
days.challenge: Identify any 'unrighteous dominion' (pride or control) in your life and repent of it today.

days.title: The Keys of the Kingdom
days.message: Priesthood keys are the authority to direct the use of the priesthood. They ensure the work is done in order.
days.challenge: Pray for your Bishop or Stake President today, recognizing the heavy keys they carry for your benefit.

days.title: The Power of Councils
days.message: The Lord works through councils. No priesthood holder is an island; we work best when we counsel with our leaders and quorums.
days.challenge: In your next meeting or family discussion, focus on listening more than you speak.

days.title: Ministering with Spirit
days.message: Ministering is not a program; it is a priesthood responsibility to watch over and strengthen each member.
days.challenge: Send a simple message of encouragement to one of the people you are assigned to watch over (or a neighbor).

days.title: Delegation and Trust
days.message: Moses learned that he couldn't do the work alone. Priesthood leadership involves empowering others to act in their own spheres.
days.challenge: Think of a task you can ask someone else to help with today to give them a chance to serve.

days.title: The Quorum Brotherhood
days.message: A quorum is more than a class; it is a brotherhood where members are bound to help one another succeed spiritually.
days.challenge: Reach out to a member of your quorum just to check in, without needing anything from them.

days.title: Personal Revelation
days.scripture: Revelation for the Church, Revelation for Our Lives
days.message: In coming days, it will not be possible to survive spiritually without the guiding influence of the Holy Ghost.
days.challenge: Ask a specific question in your prayers tonight and wait 5 minutes with a notebook to record impressions.

days.title: The Pattern of Joseph
days.message: Joseph Smith's first step to the priesthood was a simple, humble prayer. We follow that same pattern to find truth.
days.challenge: Read the account of the First Vision today and look for how God responds to humble seekers.

days.title: Nephite Ministers
days.message: Jesus gave His disciples authority to break bread and bless it. This established the order of the priesthood among the Nephites.
days.challenge: Next time you see the sacrament, focus on the specific words of the prayer and the authority behind them.

days.title: Protecting the Home
days.message: If all men were like Moroni, the powers of hell would be shaken forever. Priesthood holders are the spiritual guardians of the home.
days.challenge: Identify one 'spiritual leak' in your home (media, tone of voice, etc.) and plug it today.

days.title: Submitting to God
days.message: The 'natural man' is an enemy to God. Priesthood power requires us to be submissive, meek, humble, and patient.
days.challenge: When you feel frustrated today, consciously choose to respond with patience instead of anger.

days.title: Enduring to the End
days.message: Holding the priesthood is a lifelong marathon, not a sprint. We must press forward with a steadfastness in Christ.
days.challenge: Commit to one small spiritual habit you will not break for the rest of this 120-day journey.

days.title: Preparing for Duty
days.message: Wherefore, now let every man learn his duty, and to act in the office in which he is appointed, in all diligence.
days.challenge: Write down three specific duties of your current priesthood office from the scriptures.

days.title: The Foundation Assessment
days.message: Have you received His image in your countenance? Have you experienced this mighty change in your hearts?
days.challenge: Read through the Temple Recommend questions. Use them as a personal checklist for your spiritual foundation.

deacon.title: The Standing Minister
deacon.message: A Deacon is appointed to be a 'standing minister' to the church. This means you don't just 'do' things on Sunday; you 'are' a representative of Christ 24/7.
deacon.challenge: Identify one neighbor who might need their trash cans moved or mail brought in. Do it without being asked.

deacon.title: Assisting the Bishop
deacon.message: Deacons assist the bishopric in 'administering temporal things.' This often starts with the Fast Offering—the Lord’s way of caring for the poor.
deacon.challenge: Ask your Bishop or a parent how the church uses Fast Offerings to help people in your own city.

deacon.title: The Power of the Small
deacon.message: By small and simple things are great things brought to pass. Passing the sacrament or collecting fast offerings may seem small, but they are 'great things' to God.
deacon.challenge: Perform one 'small' task at home today (like making your bed or clearing the table) with the same care you would use at the sacrament table.

deacon.title: A Watchman on the Tower
deacon.message: A Priesthood holder is like a watchman. You notice when things are wrong and you protect the 'city' (your quorum and your family).
deacon.challenge: Pay close attention today. If you see someone being treated poorly or a situation that feels 'wrong,' move away from it or stand up for what is right.

deacon.title: The Key of Angels
deacon.message: Because you hold the keys of the ministering of angels, you are entitled to have the Lord's messengers help you in your daily life.
deacon.challenge: In your morning prayer, ask specifically for an angel (a prompt or a person) to help you make a good choice today.

deacon.title: Reliability is Power
deacon.message: The stripling warriors were 'true at all times in whatsoever thing they were entrusted.' A Deacon's greatest strength is being reliable.
deacon.challenge: Pick one thing you said you would do today and do it exactly when you said you would.

deacon.title: Sunday Reflection: The Messenger
deacon.message: Pray always, and I will pour out my Spirit upon you, and great shall be your blessing. Reflection: How has being a 'standing minister' changed your week?
deacon.challenge: Write your reflection in your journal.

deacon.title: The Temporal Steward
deacon.message: Administering to the poor is a holy stewardship. When you handle fast offerings or serve, you are doing the Lord's physical work.
deacon.challenge: Research what the 'Law of the Fast' is on the Church website for 5 minutes.

deacon.title: The Quorum Link
deacon.message: A Deacon’s quorum is a brotherhood. You are responsible for the 11 other guys in your quorum. You are linked together.
deacon.challenge: Send a 'check-in' text to one member of your quorum you haven't talked to in a while.

deacon.title: Exactness in the Ordinance
deacon.message: The Lord is a God of order. When we pass the sacrament, we do it with dignity and exactness because it represents His sacrifice.
deacon.challenge: Watch a video on the Church website about the Sacrament and look for how the Deacons show respect.

deacon.title: The Power to Resist
deacon.message: Whoso would hearken unto the word of God... the fiery darts of the adversary could not overpower them. Your priesthood is a shield.
deacon.challenge: When you feel a temptation today, touch your Priesthood ring (if you have one) or imagine your ordination to remind you of who you are.

deacon.title: A Helper of the Priest
deacon.message: Deacons are to 'assist the elder' and other offices. You are part of a team. No one serves alone in the Priesthood.
deacon.challenge: Ask a Priest or an Elder in your ward: 'Is there anything I can do to help you with your calling?'

deacon.title: Example of the Believers
deacon.message: Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example... in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity.
deacon.challenge: Focus on your 'conversation' today. Use no slang, no mean words, and no complaining for 24 hours.

deacon.title: Sunday Reflection: The Pattern
deacon.message: When ye are in the service of your fellow beings ye are only in the service of your God. Reflection: How did you serve God through people this week?
deacon.challenge: Write your reflection in your journal.

deacon.title: The Keys of the Gospel
deacon.message: The Aaronic Priesthood holds the keys of the 'gospel of repentance.' This means you have the power to help people feel they can change.
deacon.challenge: If you see a friend make a mistake, don't judge them. Be the first person to offer a 'second chance' or a kind word.

deacon.title: Preparation for the Higher
deacon.message: The Aaronic Priesthood is the 'preparatory priesthood.' It is the training ground for the Melchizedek Priesthood and a Mission.
deacon.challenge: Do one thing today that feels 'grown up'—like doing your own laundry or studying without being told.

deacon.title: The Bishop's Ears
deacon.message: Deacons can often see things the Bishop can't. You see what's happening with the other youth. You are his eyes and ears in the quorum.
deacon.challenge: If you know a youth who is struggling or sad, tell a member of the Bishopric or your Quorum Advisor.

deacon.title: The Strength of Twelve
deacon.message: A Deacon's Quorum is limited to twelve members for a reason: so you can truly know and love every single one.
deacon.challenge: Learn one new thing about a member of your quorum today (their favorite hobby or a struggle they have).

deacon.title: Honesty in the Office
deacon.message: We believe in being honest, true, chaste, benevolent, and virtuous. A Priesthood holder's word is his bond.
deacon.challenge: Be 100% honest today, even about small things that might be slightly embarrassing.

deacon.title: The Sanctification of Service
deacon.message: Whoso is faithful unto the obtaining these two priesthoods... are sanctified by the Spirit unto the renewing of their bodies.
deacon.challenge: Notice how you feel physically after you serve. The Spirit can actually give you physical energy and health.

deacon.title: Sunday Reflection: The Steward
deacon.message: He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much. Reflection: Have you been faithful in 'the least' (the small things) this week?
deacon.challenge: Write your reflection in your journal.

deacon.title: The Calling of a Deacon
deacon.message: Deacons and Teachers are to be standing ministers... to warn, expound, exhort, and teach, and invite all to come unto Christ.
deacon.challenge: If someone asks you what you did this weekend, mention that you went to church and what you learned.

deacon.title: The Power of Testimony
deacon.message: I have fasted and prayed many days that I might know these things of myself. A Deacon’s testimony is a powerful thing to the ward.
deacon.challenge: Write down 3 things you know are true about Jesus Christ. You don't have to share it, just write it for yourself.

deacon.title: The Deacon’s Presidency
deacon.message: The President of the Deacons is a high calling. He holds keys. Even if you aren't the President, you support those keys.
deacon.challenge: Pray for your Quorum President today. Ask that he may know how to lead your quorum.

deacon.title: Pure Religion
deacon.message: Pure religion... is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction. This is the Deacon's core job description.
deacon.challenge: Think of a widow or widower in your ward. Send them a card or leave a treat on their porch today.

deacon.title: Priesthood and the Home
deacon.message: Mothers and fathers are to help one another as equal partners. As a Priesthood holder, you are a partner in your home's peace.
deacon.challenge: Do the dishes or take out the trash today before anyone has the chance to ask you to do it.

deacon.title: Clean Hands, Pure Heart
deacon.message: Who shall ascend into the hill of the Lord? He that hath clean hands and a pure heart. A Deacon must stay clean to hold the sacrament.
deacon.challenge: If there is a song, a video, or a game that makes you feel 'unclean,' turn it off and don't go back to it today.

deacon.title: Sunday Reflection: The Protector
deacon.message: See that there is no iniquity in the church. Reflection: How did you protect the 'good feeling' in your home or quorum this week?
deacon.challenge: Write your reflection in your journal.

deacon.title: The Power of Quiet Service
deacon.message: That thine alms may be in secret: and thy Father which seeth in secret himself shall reward thee openly.
deacon.challenge: Do something kind for a sibling or parent and try your best not to let them find out it was you.

deacon.title: Preparation for the Temple
deacon.message: The temple is where the higher priesthood ordinances happen. Your service as a Deacon is the first step toward the temple.
deacon.challenge: Check your temple recommend. If it's expired or you don't have one, talk to your parents about making an appointment.

deacon.title: The Lord’s Representative
deacon.message: For he that is faithful and wise in time is accounted worthy to inherit the mansions prepared for him of my Father.
deacon.challenge: Imagine Jesus Christ standing next to you for the next hour. How would you act? Do that for the whole hour.

deacon.title: Month 2 Mastery Reflection
deacon.message: He that is found worthy shall stand. You have completed the study of the Office of a Deacon. What have you learned about yourself?
deacon.challenge: Share one thing you've learned this month with your Bishop or your Dad.

teacher.title: Watching Over the Church
teacher.message: The Teacher’s duty is to 'watch over the church always, and be with and strengthen them.' This means you are a spiritual lookout, noticing who is struggling and who needs a friend.
teacher.challenge: Scan the room at your next school or church event. Identify one person sitting alone and make an effort to be with and strengthen them.

teacher.title: The Peacemaker's Authority
teacher.message: Teachers are specifically charged to see that there is 'no hardness with each other.' You have a priesthood mandate to be a peacemaker and resolve conflicts.
teacher.challenge: If you hear someone being criticized today, use your influence to stop the gossip or say something positive about that person.

teacher.title: Strengthening the Quorum
teacher.message: To 'strengthen' means to make someone more able to resist pressure. Your friendship can be the 'spiritual bracing' that helps a quorum member stay strong.
teacher.challenge: Text a friend in your quorum and share a funny or uplifting thought just to strengthen your bond.

teacher.title: No Iniquity in the Church
teacher.message: As a Teacher, you help ensure members live the standards. This starts with you. You cannot lead someone to a place you are not willing to go yourself.
teacher.challenge: Evaluate your own 'hardness.' Is there someone you are holding a grudge against? Decide today to let it go.

teacher.title: The Power of Presence
teacher.message: The scripture says Teachers should 'be with' the members. Sometimes the most powerful priesthood service is simply showing up and being present for someone.
teacher.challenge: Put your phone away entirely during a conversation today. Give that person your full, undivided 'priesthood presence'.

teacher.title: An Example of Believers
teacher.message: As a Teacher, you are no longer the 'youngest' in the Aaronic Priesthood. Deacons are watching you. Your example is now a form of leadership.
teacher.challenge: Think of one 'Deacon-age' boy you know. Set a high standard of reverence or kindness today that he can follow.

teacher.title: Sunday Reflection: The Lookout
teacher.message: Obey them that have the rule over you... for they watch for your souls. Reflection: How did you 'watch for souls' this week?
teacher.challenge: Write your reflection in your journal.

teacher.title: Preparing the Table
teacher.message: Teachers have the sacred responsibility to prepare the bread and water for the sacrament. You are preparing the emblems of the Savior's Atonement.
teacher.challenge: The next time you prepare the sacrament, do it in total silence. Focus on the fact that you are preparing a 'feast' for the souls of the ward.

teacher.title: A Messenger of Truth
teacher.message: Teachers are to 'warn, expound, exhort, and teach.' This requires you to know the doctrine. You cannot teach what you do not know.
teacher.challenge: Spend 10 minutes today studying one 'Gospel Topic' on the Church website so you are prepared to expound it if asked.

teacher.title: The Spirit of Warning
teacher.message: To 'warn' doesn't mean to be mean; it means to care enough about someone to tell them they are heading for danger. It is an act of love.
teacher.challenge: If a friend is making a choice that you know will hurt them, find a kind, private way to share your concern today.

teacher.title: The Law of the Fast
teacher.message: Fasting is a way to 'offer your whole souls as an offering unto Him.' Teachers often help collect these offerings to care for the poor.
teacher.challenge: Prepare for the next Fast Sunday by writing down one spiritual question you want answered during your fast.

teacher.title: Assisting the Priest
teacher.message: Teachers are a bridge between Deacons and Priests. You assist the Priests in their duties, learning the 'higher' ordinances while mastering the 'preparatory' ones.
teacher.challenge: Ask a Priest today if you can help him with any of his responsibilities or ministering assignments.

teacher.title: The Power of Persuasion
teacher.message: No power or influence can or ought to be maintained... only by persuasion. A Teacher doesn't force; he invites and persuades.
teacher.challenge: Instead of telling someone what to do today, try to 'persuade' them by explaining the 'why' behind the request.

teacher.title: Sunday Reflection: The Peacemaker
teacher.message: Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God. Reflection: Where did you bring peace this week?
teacher.challenge: Write your reflection in your journal.

teacher.title: The Teacher's Quorum
teacher.message: A Teacher's Quorum is presided over by a President who holds keys. Unity in the quorum is the Teacher's primary social responsibility.
teacher.challenge: Identify one member of your quorum who seems 'quiet' or 'distant.' Make a plan to include them in the next activity.

teacher.title: Reliability in Preparation
teacher.message: Learn his duty, and to act in the office in which he is appointed, in all diligence. Diligence in preparation makes the ordinance sacred.
teacher.challenge: Be the first person to arrive to help prepare the sacrament (or any other assignment) this week.

teacher.title: The Ministering Brother
teacher.message: Teachers are often assigned as ministering companions to Elders. You are learning how to 'mourn with those that mourn' at a professional level.
teacher.challenge: Ask your ministering companion if you can share a short scripture or thought during your next visit or message.

teacher.title: Standing in Holy Places
teacher.message: A Teacher must stand in holy places so he can recognize when 'iniquity' is trying to enter the church or his own life.
teacher.challenge: Refine your environment today. Delete one song or social media follow that doesn't feel 'holy' to you.

teacher.title: The Authority of Invitation
teacher.message: You are to 'invite all to come unto Christ.' This isn't just for missionaries. It is the daily duty of every Teacher.
teacher.challenge: Invite a friend to join you for an upcoming youth activity or a Sunday meeting.

teacher.title: The Keys of the Preparatory Priesthood
teacher.message: The Aaronic Priesthood holds the keys of the ministering of angels. As a Teacher, you can be an 'angelic' influence in your home.
teacher.challenge: Do an anonymous act of service for a sibling today—something that makes their life easier without them knowing why.

teacher.title: Sunday Reflection: The Guardian
teacher.message: See that the members do their duty. Reflection: How did you encourage someone else to keep their covenants this week?
teacher.challenge: Write your reflection in your journal.

teacher.title: Meekness in Leadership
teacher.message: A Teacher must be 'submissive, meek, humble, patient, full of love.' This is how you gain influence, not through being the 'loudest' in the room.
teacher.challenge: In a group setting today, wait until everyone else has spoken before you share your opinion.

teacher.title: The Armor of God
teacher.message: Teachers are on the 'front lines' of watching over the church. You need your armor on every day to be an effective guardian.
teacher.challenge: Put on your 'spiritual armor' tonight by reading your scriptures for 10 minutes before bed.

teacher.title: Teaching by the Spirit
teacher.message: If ye receive not the Spirit ye shall not teach. A Teacher's words only have power if the Spirit is carrying them into the heart.
teacher.challenge: Before you speak to anyone about the gospel today, say a quick silent prayer for the Spirit to guide your words.

teacher.title: The Strength of the Quorum Presidency
teacher.message: The Teacher's presidency leads the quorum. Whether you are in the presidency or not, your support determines the quorum's power.
teacher.challenge: Reach out to your Quorum President today and ask: 'What is one goal we have for the quorum that I can help with?'

teacher.title: Watching Over Your Family
teacher.message: The first place a Teacher 'watches over the church' is within the walls of his own home. You are a guardian of your family's spirit.
teacher.challenge: Offer to lead the family prayer or the scripture study tonight.

teacher.title: Exactness and Honor
teacher.message: Every man should take righteousness in his hands... and lift up a warning voice. To be a Teacher is to be an honorable man.
teacher.challenge: Identify one area where you have been 'slack' (lazy) in your priesthood duties and fix it today.

teacher.title: Sunday Reflection: The Peacemaker
teacher.message: Blessed are the peacemakers. Reflection: How did you handle a conflict or 'hardness' this week?
teacher.challenge: Write your reflection in your journal.

teacher.title: The Power of the Aaronic Priesthood
teacher.message: I will use the priesthood to serve others, beginning in my home. A Teacher's power comes from his willingness to serve.
teacher.challenge: Recite the Aaronic Priesthood Quorum Theme (or read it) and choose one phrase to live by today.

teacher.title: Preparing for the Priest's Office
teacher.message: Soon you will hold the authority to baptize and bless the sacrament. Your time as a Teacher is to prepare your heart for that weight.
teacher.challenge: Read about the duties of a Priest today. What is one thing you are excited to do when you are ordained?

teacher.title: A Watchman's Reward
teacher.message: They become the sons of Moses and of Aaron and the seed of Abraham, and the church and kingdom, and the elect of God.
teacher.challenge: Think about the future 'High Priest' you will become. Write a short note to your future self about why you chose to stay worthy today.

teacher.title: Month 2 Mastery Reflection
teacher.message: He that is found worthy shall stand. You have completed the study of the Office of a Teacher. How has your 'watch' gone this month?
teacher.challenge: Share your biggest 'Aha!' moment from this month with your Quorum Advisor or Bishop.

priest.title: The Authority to Baptize
priest.message: A Priest has the authority to baptize. This is the act of opening the gate to the Kingdom of God for another soul. It is a sacred, heavy trust that requires absolute worthiness.
priest.challenge: Visualize yourself performing a baptism. Reflect on the worthiness required to hold a soul under the water and bring them up to a new life.

priest.title: Administering the Sacrament
priest.message: When a Priest kneels to pray over the sacrament, he is the voice of the entire congregation to the Father. You are pleading for the Spirit to be with everyone in the room.
priest.challenge: Read the sacrament prayers in D&C 20:77, 79. Note the specific promises we make. Try to memorize the prayer for the bread today.

priest.title: Preach, Teach, and Expound
priest.message: Priests are commanded to 'preach, teach, expound, and exhort.' This means you aren't just a helper; you are a primary teacher of the gospel.
priest.challenge: Choose one gospel principle (like Faith or Repentance) and explain it out loud to yourself or a family member for 2 minutes.

priest.title: Visiting the House of Each Member
priest.message: The Lord specifically charges Priests to visit the house of each member and exhort them to pray vocally and in secret. This is the scriptural root of ministering.
priest.challenge: Reach out to one person you minister to. Don't just text—ask if you can share a 1-minute spiritual thought with them this week.

priest.title: The Spirit of Elijah
priest.message: The Aaronic Priesthood is closely tied to the gathering of Israel. As a Priest, you are preparing to do the work of the temple and family history.
priest.challenge: Find one name on FamilySearch that needs temple work done. If you can't find one, ask a consultant to help you for 10 minutes.

priest.title: The Power of the Spoken Word
priest.message: Priests are to 'inform the church' of their duties. Your words have weight. When you speak in meetings or in private, people should feel the Lord's influence.
priest.challenge: Make a goal to not use any 'filler' words (like, um, uh) today. Speak with purpose and clarity.

priest.title: Sunday Reflection: The Ordinance
priest.message: In the ordinances thereof, the power of godliness is manifest. Reflection: Did you feel the 'power of godliness' while officiating today?
priest.challenge: Write your reflection in your journal.

priest.title: The Office of an Elder
priest.message: When there is no Elder present, the Priest takes the lead. You are the bridge to the Melchizedek Priesthood. You must be ready to lead at any moment.
priest.challenge: Identify a situation where leadership is needed today (at home or school) and quietly step up to fill the gap.

priest.title: A Messenger of Repentance
priest.message: Holding the keys of the gospel of repentance means you are a specialist in 'second chances.' You help people feel they can return to God.
priest.challenge: Is there someone you have been judgmental toward? Use your 'keys of repentance' to forgive them and start fresh today.

priest.title: The Dignity of the Table
priest.message: You cannot partake of the Lord's table and the table of devils. A Priest's life must be consistent. What you do on Saturday night affects Sunday morning.
priest.challenge: Evaluate your entertainment choices for the last 48 hours. Is there anything that would make you feel awkward kneeling at the sacrament table?

priest.title: Ordaining Others
priest.message: Priests have the authority to ordain other Priests, Teachers, and Deacons. You are part of the chain of authority passing the power to the next generation.
priest.challenge: Study the ordinance of 'Ordination' in the General Handbook Chapter 18 today so you are prepared to assist.

priest.title: The Duty to Exhort
priest.message: To 'exhort' is to strongly encourage or urge someone to follow a righteous path. It is more than just being 'nice'; it is being a bold friend.
priest.challenge: Encourage a friend today to keep a standard or a commandment that they might be tempted to break.

priest.title: The Savior’s Hands
priest.message: Jesus gave His disciples the power to break bread and bless it. When you do the same, you are acting as His literal hands for the ward.
priest.challenge: Next time you break the bread, do it with the thought: 'This is a physical representation of the Savior's body.' Do it with reverence.

priest.title: Sunday Reflection: The Voice
priest.message: Whether by mine own voice or by the voice of my servants, it is the same. Reflection: How does it feel to know that when you bless the sacrament, it is as if the Lord said the words?
priest.challenge: Write your reflection in your journal.

priest.title: The Bishop’s Quorum
priest.message: The Bishop is the President of the Priests Quorum. He sits in council with you directly. You have a closer link to the 'Judge in Israel' than anyone else.
priest.challenge: During your next quorum meeting, pay close attention to the Bishop's face and tone. What is he most concerned about? How can you help?

priest.title: Preparing for a Mission
priest.message: If ye have desires to serve God ye are called to the work. The office of a Priest is the final training ground for full-time missionary service.
priest.challenge: Practice explaining the Restoration to a parent or friend for 3 minutes today. Use a scripture.

priest.title: The Key of Knowledge
priest.message: The higher priesthood holds the key of the knowledge of God. As a Priest, you are reaching for that key. You should be seeking deeper answers in your study.
priest.challenge: Go beyond your normal scripture reading today. Look up a word in the Bible Dictionary or Topical Guide and follow the links.

priest.title: Watching Over the Church
priest.message: Priests, like Teachers, are to watch over the church. But Priests often do this with more maturity and a broader range of influence.
priest.challenge: Identify a family in the ward that is going through a hard time. Pray for them specifically and ask how you can help.

priest.title: The Law of the Fast
priest.message: The children of God were commanded to gather together oft, and join in fasting and mighty prayer in behalf of the welfare of the souls.
priest.challenge: The next time you fast, do it specifically for someone else's 'welfare' rather than your own needs.

priest.title: Example in Speech
priest.message: Let no corrupt communication proceed out of your mouth, but that which is good to the use of edifying. A Priest's mouth is for blessing, not cursing.
priest.challenge: Remove all sarcasm and 'edgy' humor from your speech today. Focus purely on 'edifying' others.

priest.title: Sunday Reflection: The Covenant
priest.message: That they may always have his Spirit to be with them. Reflection: How did your actions this week invite or offend the Spirit?
priest.challenge: Write your reflection in your journal.

priest.title: The Ministering of Angels
priest.message: You hold the keys of the ministering of angels. This means you have a right to receive messages from the other side of the veil to help you in your duties.
priest.challenge: In a quiet moment today, ask: 'Is there anyone the Lord wants me to help?' Wait and see if a name or face comes to mind.

priest.title: Pure Religion in Action
priest.message: To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction. Priests have the physical strength and authority to really make a difference for those in need.
priest.challenge: Offer to do 30 minutes of physical labor for a widow, a single parent, or someone sick in your ward today.

priest.title: Priesthood and the Future
priest.message: Whoso is faithful unto the obtaining these two priesthoods... are sanctified by the Spirit. You are almost at the 'two priesthoods' mark.
priest.challenge: Write down 3 ways you want your life to change once you receive the Melchizedek Priesthood.

priest.title: Teaching with Power
priest.message: They had taught with power and authority of God. This power came because they 'searched the scriptures diligently.'
priest.challenge: Pick one chapter in the Book of Mormon and study it until you feel you could teach a 10-minute lesson on it.

priest.title: The Guardian of the Home
priest.message: Let thy bowels also be full of charity towards all men, and to the household of faith. A Priest is the spiritual backup for his father.
priest.challenge: Ask your father (or mother): 'How can I better support the spiritual feeling in our home?'

priest.title: Exactness in Ritual
priest.message: The Lord gave specific words for baptism. Exactness shows our submissiveness to God's ways rather than our own.
priest.challenge: Read the baptismal prayer. Think about why the Lord requires that specific set of words and no other.

priest.title: Sunday Reflection: The Steward
priest.message: Wherefore, now let every man learn his duty. Reflection: What 'duty' did you learn this month that you didn't know before?
priest.challenge: Write your reflection in your journal.

priest.title: The Strength of the Aaronic Priesthood
priest.message: I will prepare to become a diligent missionary, loyal husband, and loving father. These are your next three 'offices' in life.
priest.challenge: Choose one word from the quorum theme (Loyal, Loving, Diligent) and be that word today.

priest.title: The Call to Serve
priest.message: Therefore, if ye have desires to serve God ye are called to the work. Your desire is the first step to your mission call.
priest.challenge: Spend 5 minutes tonight imagining your mission. Ask the Lord to help you develop the specific talent you will need there.

priest.title: A Life of Holiness
priest.message: Every member... shall manifest by a youthful walk and conversation, that they are worthy of it. A Priest's walk should be different from the world's.
priest.challenge: Walk and talk today as if you were already wearing a missionary name tag. Notice how people treat you differently.

priest.title: Month 2 Mastery Reflection
priest.message: He that is found worthy shall stand. You have completed the study of the Office of a Priest. What is the greatest lesson you've learned?
priest.challenge: Share your biggest spiritual 'win' from this month with your Bishop in your next interview.

elder.title: A Standing Minister
elder.message: Elders are appointed to be 'standing ministers' to the church. Unlike a missionary who moves on, a standing minister is a constant, local source of spiritual power and stability for his family and neighbors.
elder.challenge: Identify one neighbor or ward member who is currently 'struggling in the wind.' Commit to being a steady, prayerful support for them this week.

elder.title: The Oath and Covenant
elder.message: When you received the Melchizedek Priesthood, you entered into a covenant with God that He reinforced with an Oath. He cannot break it. Your power is directly tied to how you 'receive' the Lord's servants and His word.
elder.challenge: Read D&C 84:33-40. List the specific things the Lord promises to give you as you magnify your calling. Which promise do you need most right now?

elder.title: The Power to Confirm
elder.message: An Elder has the authority to bestow the Gift of the Holy Ghost. You are a conduit for the Comforter. This requires you to live in a way that the Spirit is never a stranger to you.
elder.challenge: Reflect on a time you felt the Holy Ghost guide you. Share that experience with a family member or write it in your journal today.

elder.title: Ministering by the Spirit
elder.message: Ministering is more than a visit; it is a spiritual stewardship. An Elder seeks to know the needs of those he serves through the lens of the Spirit, not just a checklist.
elder.challenge: Pray for your ministering families by name today. Ask the Lord: 'What is one thing they are not telling me that they need help with?'

elder.title: The Key of Knowledge
elder.message: The Melchizedek Priesthood holds the 'key of the knowledge of God.' This means you have a right to receive revelation to understand the mysteries and the heart of God.
elder.challenge: Take a difficult question you’ve had about the gospel to the Lord today. Study the scriptures and wait for a 'key' of insight to turn.

elder.title: Leading in the Home
elder.message: The home is the most important place an Elder exercises his priesthood. It must be done by persuasion, long-suffering, gentleness, and meekness—never by 'unrighteous dominion.'
elder.challenge: Identify a moment today where you feel frustrated with a family member. Intentionally choose 'gentleness' and 'meekness' instead of raising your voice.

elder.title: Sunday Reflection: The Holy Order
elder.message: This high priesthood being after the order of his Son. Reflection: How has remembering that you hold the 'Priesthood of the Son of God' changed your behavior this week?
elder.challenge: Write your reflection in your journal.

elder.title: The Duty to Bless
elder.message: Is any sick among you? Let him call for the elders. An Elder is a healer. While the medicine may be physical, the spiritual comfort and healing come through the priesthood.
elder.challenge: Review the instructions for 'Anointing and Sealing the Sick' in the Handbook today. Ensure you are ready to perform this ordinance tonight if called upon.

elder.title: The Power of Councils
elder.message: Elders work in quorums and councils. Revelation is scattered among the group. Your job is to speak your mind with humility and listen with intent.
elder.challenge: In your next meeting or family discussion, ask: 'What do you think?' to someone who hasn't spoken yet.

elder.title: The Law of the Fast
elder.message: The Fast is designed to 'loose the bands of wickedness' and 'deal thy bread to the hungry.' An Elder oversees the spiritual health of his community by how he honors the fast.
elder.challenge: Increase your next fast offering by a small amount, or find a specific way to physically 'deal bread' to someone in need today.

elder.title: The Power of Godliness
elder.message: In the ordinances of the Melchizedek Priesthood, the 'power of godliness' is manifest. Every time you participate in an ordinance, you are bringing the power of God into the room.
elder.challenge: The next time you stand in a priesthood circle, focus on the words being said. Try to feel the 'godliness' being invoked.

elder.title: Charity: The Engine of Power
elder.message: Charity is the pure love of Christ. Without it, an Elder's priesthood is 'sounding brass.' It is the only influence that endures beyond the veil.
elder.challenge: Pray with all the energy of your heart today to be filled with this love for someone you currently find 'unlovable'.

elder.title: Diligence in Stewardship
elder.message: Learn his duty, and to act in the office in which he is appointed. Slothfulness is the primary enemy of priesthood power. An Elder must be active, not passive.
elder.challenge: Identify one priesthood duty you have been 'slothful' in (ministering, study, or home duties) and tackle it first thing today.

elder.title: Sunday Reflection: The Steward
elder.message: For it is required of every steward to render an account. Reflection: If you had to report your stewardship to the Lord tonight, what would you be most proud of this week?
elder.challenge: Write your reflection in your journal.

elder.title: The Patriarchal Order
elder.message: Abraham sought the 'blessings of the fathers' and the 'right to be ordained' to the higher priesthood. You are part of a line of righteous men that stretches back to Adam.
elder.challenge: Look at your Priesthood Line of Authority today. Pray for the men who laid hands on your head to ordain you.

elder.title: Succoring the Weak
elder.message: Succor the weak, lift up the hands which hang down, and strengthen the feeble knees. This is the definition of the Elder's daily mission.
elder.challenge: Reach out to a ward member who is physically or emotionally 'feeble' right now. Offer a specific act of service (a ride, a meal, or a listening ear).

elder.title: The Presence of the Comforter
elder.message: An Elder is never alone. The Comforter is your companion. In every blessing and every lesson, He is the one doing the heavy lifting.
elder.challenge: In a difficult conversation today, pause and ask the Spirit: 'What does this person need to feel from me right now?'

elder.title: Magnifying the Calling
elder.message: To magnify is to make larger. You take your small, human efforts and, through the Priesthood, the Lord makes them large enough to save souls.
elder.challenge: Do one 'small' act of service today (like a kind text) but do it with the 'magnified' intent of a Priesthood holder.

elder.title: The Duty to Teach
elder.message: Elders are to teach, expound, exhort, baptize, and watch over the church. You are a teacher by divine appointment.
elder.challenge: Find an opportunity to share a gospel truth today—perhaps with your children, a coworker, or a friend.

elder.title: Clean Hands, Pure Heart
elder.message: An Elder cannot lift others to higher ground if he is sinking in the mire. Personal purity is the bedrock of your authority.
elder.challenge: Identify one 'grey area' in your life (media, thoughts, or habits) and decide today to make it 'white' and pure.

elder.title: Sunday Reflection: The Keeper
elder.message: Am I my brother's keeper? For an Elder, the answer is a resounding 'Yes.' Reflection: How did you 'keep' your brothers and sisters this week?
elder.challenge: Write your reflection in your journal.

elder.title: The Burden of the Keys
elder.message: While many Elders do not hold keys, all act under the direction of those who do. Following keys is the way we stay aligned with the Lord's will.
elder.challenge: Express support to your Quorum President or Bishop today. Let them know you are ready to serve under their direction.

elder.title: The Savior’s Example
elder.message: Hold up your light that it may shine unto the world. Behold I am the light which ye shall hold up. You are the lamp; He is the light.
elder.challenge: Be a 'lamp' today. Perform an act of service that is so clearly 'Christian' that people notice the Light, not just you.

elder.title: Sanctified by the Spirit
elder.message: Faithfulness in the Priesthood results in the 'renewing of their bodies.' There is a physical and spiritual vitality that comes from serving the Lord.
elder.challenge: Notice your energy levels today as you serve. Do you feel a 'renewal' of spirit when you are about the Lord's business?

elder.title: The Power of Persuasion
elder.message: Real priesthood influence is never forced. It is built over time through consistent, quiet persuasion and love unfeigned.
elder.challenge: Instead of demanding or expecting something today, try to 'persuade' with kindness and explanation.

elder.title: The Eternal Perspective
elder.message: Thy dominion shall be an everlasting dominion. What you do as an Elder has consequences that reach into the eternities.
elder.challenge: Think about one person you serve. Imagine them in the Celestial Kingdom. How would you treat them right now if you saw them that way?

elder.title: Reliability in the Kingdom
elder.message: True at all times in whatsoever thing they were entrusted. An Elder's greatest asset to a Bishop is being someone who simply gets it done.
elder.challenge: Complete a task you've been putting off for a week. Do it with 100% excellence.

elder.title: Sunday Reflection: The Peacemaker
elder.message: Blessed are the peacemakers. Reflection: How did you bring the peace of the Melchizedek Priesthood into a tense situation this week?
elder.challenge: Write your reflection in your journal.

elder.title: The Higher Law
elder.message: Therefore I would that ye should be perfect even as I. An Elder is reaching for the standard of the Savior—perfection through His grace.
elder.challenge: Pick one 'small' habit you know is beneath your potential and replace it with a higher standard today.

elder.title: Prepared to Officiate
elder.message: High priests... have a right to officiate in their own standing... and also in the office of an elder. You are part of a grand hierarchy of service.
elder.challenge: Study the duties of a High Priest today. How does your current service as an Elder prepare you for even greater responsibilities?

elder.title: A Life of Consecration
elder.message: Every man seeking the interest of his neighbor, and doing all things with an eye single to the glory of God.
elder.challenge: Do one thing today purely for the 'interest of your neighbor' without any thought of how it benefits you.

elder.title: Month 2 Mastery Reflection
elder.message: He that is found worthy shall stand. You have completed the study of the Office of an Elder. What is the biggest shift in your heart?
elder.challenge: Review your month. Write down the one 'spiritual discovery' that has changed your priesthood service forever.

high_Priest.title: Spiritual Administration
high_Priest.message: High Priests have a right to officiate in all the offices of the church. Your role is one of spiritual administration—ensuring the 'power of godliness' is manifest in every ordinance and meeting.
high_Priest.challenge: Identify one meeting or project you are involved in. Pray specifically that you can bring a 'spiritual' rather than just 'administrative' influence to it today.

high_Priest.title: The Holy Order
high_Priest.message: High Priests were ordained after the 'Holy Order' from the foundation of the world. This is not a title of status, but a calling of preparation for others to see the Son of God.
high_Priest.challenge: Contemplate the phrase 'prepared from the foundation of the world.' How does this perspective change how you view your current ward responsibilities?

high_Priest.title: A High Priest of Good Things
high_Priest.message: Christ is the 'high priest of good things to come.' As a High Priest, you should be a source of optimism and hope. You look past current trials to the 'good things' the Lord has promised.
high_Priest.challenge: When a ward member or friend complains about a trial today, offer a perspective of hope based on the promises of the gospel.

high_Priest.title: The Right to Preside
high_Priest.message: High Priests have the authority to preside. Presiding is not about control; it is about creating a space where others can receive revelation. It is the art of spiritual leadership.
high_Priest.challenge: In a family or church setting today, practice presiding by asking: 'What is the Spirit telling us we should do?' rather than giving your own solution first.

high_Priest.title: The Key of Knowledge
high_Priest.message: The Melchizedek Priesthood holds the 'key of the knowledge of God.' As a High Priest, you are expected to be a deep student of the word, capable of 'expounding' the mysteries of the kingdom.
high_Priest.challenge: Study a difficult chapter in the New Testament or Doctrine & Covenants today for 20 minutes. Don't stop until you feel you've gained one new 'key' of understanding.

high_Priest.title: A Father in Israel
high_Priest.message: You may have ten thousand instructors, but not many fathers. A High Priest often acts as a spiritual father to those in his ward, providing wisdom and stable love.
high_Priest.challenge: Reach out to a younger man (perhaps a Priest or Elder) and offer a sincere word of encouragement about his potential.

high_Priest.title: Sunday Reflection: The Order of Melchizedek
high_Priest.message: Melchizedek was a man of such faith that he 'wrought righteousness' and 'stopped the mouths of lions.' Reflection: How is your faith affecting the 'righteousness' of your home?
high_Priest.challenge: Write your reflection in your journal.

high_Priest.title: Counseling with Equity
high_Priest.message: The High Priest sits in council to handle matters with equity and justice. This requires a heart free from prejudice and a mind focused on the Lord's will.
high_Priest.challenge: If you are involved in a disagreement today, try to see the 'equity' (fairness) for all sides before forming a judgment.

high_Priest.title: A Pillar of Stability
high_Priest.message: In the early church, some were seen as 'pillars.' High Priests are the pillars of the ward—they stay firm when the 'weather' of life gets rough.
high_Priest.challenge: Identify a 'storm' someone you know is facing. Be their 'pillar' today by offering steady, calm reassurance that the Lord is in control.

high_Priest.title: The Oath and Covenant
high_Priest.message: Because you have received the high priesthood, God has sworn an oath to give you 'all that my Father hath.' The weight of this promise should inspire total consecration.
high_Priest.challenge: Read the Oath and Covenant of the Priesthood. What is the one thing you are still holding back from the Lord? Give it to Him today.

high_Priest.title: The Power of Godliness
high_Priest.message: Without the ordinances and the authority of the priesthood, the 'power of godliness' is not manifest. You are a steward of this manifestation.
high_Priest.challenge: Prepare to participate in an ordinance (even if it's just the sacrament) by spending 10 minutes in quiet meditation on the Savior's Atonement.

high_Priest.title: Teaching the Children of Men
high_Priest.message: High Priests are ordained to 'teach his commandments unto the children of men.' Your life is a constant lesson to those around you.
high_Priest.challenge: Identify one commandment you find beautiful. Find a natural way to talk about why you love keeping that commandment today.

high_Priest.title: Meekness in High Office
high_Priest.message: Moses was 'very meek, above all the men which were upon the face of the earth.' The more authority you hold, the more meek you must become.
high_Priest.challenge: In a situation where you could easily 'take charge' today, choose to serve behind the scenes and let someone else take the credit.

high_Priest.title: Sunday Reflection: The Steward
high_Priest.message: It is required of every steward to render an account. Reflection: If you gave your weekly account to the Lord today, how would you describe your care for 'the one'?
high_Priest.challenge: Write your reflection in your journal.

high_Priest.title: The Patriarchal Link
high_Priest.message: High Priests are part of a lineage of 'fathers' that goes back to the beginning. You are a link in a chain of righteousness that spans millennia.
high_Priest.challenge: Look at your family tree. Identify one 'Priesthood Father' (ancestor) and learn one story about their faith today.

high_Priest.title: Succoring the Weak
high_Priest.message: A High Priest must have the strength to 'succor the weak' and 'lift up the hands which hang down.' This requires physical and spiritual stamina.
high_Priest.challenge: Who in your ward has 'feeble knees' (is discouraged)? Send them a note or visit them with the sole intent of strengthening them.

high_Priest.title: The Comforter as a Partner
high_Priest.message: In the High Priesthood, you are never alone. The Holy Ghost is your administrative partner, revealing what needs to be said and done.
high_Priest.challenge: Before you enter your home or a meeting today, pray: 'Spirit, guide my influence.' Watch for the subtle promptings that follow.

high_Priest.title: Magnifying the Calling
high_Priest.message: To magnify is to make the Lord's work look larger through your small lens. You represent the Savior's kingdom to the world.
high_Priest.challenge: Choose one 'routine' task today and do it with such excellence and kindness that people see the 'Priesthood' in the quality of your work.

high_Priest.title: The Spirit of Elijah
high_Priest.message: High Priests are deeply involved in the gathering of Israel on both sides of the veil. The keys of this dispensation are yours to support.
high_Priest.challenge: Spend 15 minutes on FamilySearch today. Find a name or a memory that connects you to the 'fathers'.

high_Priest.title: The Example of the Believers
high_Priest.message: Even as an experienced High Priest, you must be an 'example of the believers.' People watch how you handle stress, success, and sorrow.
high_Priest.challenge: In a moment of stress today, intentionally react with the patience and calm you would expect from a prophet.

high_Priest.title: Sunday Reflection: The Keeper
high_Priest.message: Melchizedek... did establish peace in the land in his days. Reflection: How did you act as a 'Prince of Peace' in your ward or home this week?
high_Priest.challenge: Write your reflection in your journal.

high_Priest.title: Unrighteous Dominion
high_Priest.message: The temptation of the High Priesthood is to exercise 'unrighteous dominion' because of years of experience. Authority only exists by love unfeigned.
high_Priest.challenge: Ask your wife or a close friend: 'Do I ever make you feel like your opinion doesn't matter?' Listen to their answer without defending yourself.

high_Priest.title: The Power of Persuasion
high_Priest.message: A High Priest leads through the power of persuasion, not position. If you have to remind someone of your title, you have already lost your power.
high_Priest.challenge: Try to get someone to help you with a task today using only 'gentleness' and 'meekness' and 'long-suffering'.

high_Priest.title: Sanctified by the Spirit
high_Priest.message: Faithfulness in the Priesthood results in the 'renewing of their bodies.' There is a physical and spiritual vitality that comes from being a 'High Priest of good things.'
high_Priest.challenge: Notice your energy levels as you do the Lord's work. Does it 'renew' you or drain you? Ask the Lord to help you find joy in the labor.

high_Priest.title: Watching Over the Souls
high_Priest.message: High Priests watch for the souls of the people 'as they that must give account.' You are a spiritual guardian of the ward family.
high_Priest.challenge: Scan your ward directory today. Stop at the first name that 'feels' like they need a prayer. Pray for their soul specifically.

high_Priest.title: The Duty to Bless
high_Priest.message: An high priest... is to minister in spiritual things. Your primary duty is to be a source of blessing to everyone you encounter.
high_Priest.challenge: Offer a sincere, verbal blessing (or a prayer of blessing) for someone in your family today who is struggling with a decision.

high_Priest.title: Reliability in the Holy Order
high_Priest.message: The stripling warriors were 'true at all times.' A High Priest’s reliability is the bedrock upon which the Bishop and Quorum President build.
high_Priest.challenge: Complete a 'dull' administrative task today with 100% accuracy and ahead of schedule.

high_Priest.title: Sunday Reflection: The Intercessor
high_Priest.message: He ever liveth to make intercession for them. Reflection: How did you act as an 'intercessor' for someone in your care this week?
high_Priest.challenge: Write your reflection in your journal.

high_Priest.title: The Higher Law of Love
high_Priest.message: Love your enemies, bless them that curse you. A High Priest has lived long enough to know that love is the only permanent solution to any problem.
high_Priest.challenge: Identify a 'rival' or someone you dislike. Do something genuinely kind for them or their family today.

high_Priest.title: The Unchanging Scepter
high_Priest.message: Thy scepter an unchanging scepter of righteousness and truth. In a world of shifting values, a High Priest remains unchanged in his integrity.
high_Priest.challenge: Commit to one 'unchanging' standard of truth today, even if it is unpopular in your workplace or social circle.

high_Priest.title: Prepared for the Presence
high_Priest.message: For without this no man can see the face of God... and live. The High Priesthood is the preparation for the ultimate presence.
high_Priest.challenge: In your evening prayer tonight, speak to God as if you were literally in His presence. Be that honest and that reverent.

high_Priest.title: Month 2 Mastery Reflection
high_Priest.message: He that is found worthy shall stand. You have completed the study of the Office of a High Priest. What have you learned about the 'Holy Order'?
high_Priest.challenge: Review your month. Write down the one 'administrative' habit you are replacing with a 'spiritual' one from now on.

deacon.title: The Power of the Aaronic Priesthood
deacon.message: The power and authority of the lesser, or Aaronic Priesthood, is to hold the keys of the ministering of angels. This is not a symbolic power; it is a literal right to heavenly help.
deacon.challenge: Before you leave your house today, pray specifically for 'angelic' protection or guidance for someone you know is having a hard time.

deacon.title: The Law of the Fast
deacon.message: Fasting is a law of power. For a Deacon, collecting fast offerings is how you help the Bishop 'loose the bands of wickedness.' The physical act of walking door-to-door (or serving) is a spiritual sacrifice.
deacon.challenge: Think of one thing you 'crave' (a snack, a game, or a habit). Give it up for 24 hours as a small 'fast' to strengthen your will.

deacon.title: Angels are Not Always Invisible
deacon.message: The scripture says some have entertained angels 'unawares.' As a Deacon holding those keys, you are often the 'angel' someone else has been praying for.
deacon.challenge: Listen for a 'whisper' today to do something kind. If a name pops into your head, act on it immediately. That is you using your keys.

deacon.title: The Power of Silence
deacon.message: Be still and know that I am God. A Deacon learns to hear the Spirit in the quiet moments—like while passing the sacrament or sitting in a quorum meeting.
deacon.challenge: Find 5 minutes of total silence today. No phone, no music. Just sit and ask the Lord: 'What do You want me to know?'

deacon.title: Reliability is a Spiritual Gift
deacon.message: The 2,000 stripling warriors were 'true at all times.' In the Priesthood, 'showing up' is 90% of the battle. The Lord can work through a boy He can count on.
deacon.challenge: If you have an assignment this Sunday, double-check the time. If you don't, ask your leader: 'Where do you need me most?'

deacon.title: The Power of Pure Speech
deacon.message: Out of the same mouth proceedeth blessing and cursing. My brethren, these things ought not so to be. A Deacon's voice is the voice of the Priesthood.
deacon.challenge: Eliminate all slang and 'borderline' bad words today. Speak only words that would be appropriate in the Celestial Kingdom.

deacon.title: The Key of Repentance
deacon.message: The Aaronic Priesthood holds the 'Gospel of Repentance.' This means you have the power to invite people to change. It starts by you being the first to say 'I'm sorry.'
deacon.challenge: Think of a small conflict you’ve had recently. Even if it wasn't your fault, be the one to apologize or offer a 'reset' to that person.

deacon.title: A Steward of the Poor
deacon.message: To retain a remission of your sins, you must 'impart of your substance to the poor.' Deacons are the front line of this covenant.
deacon.challenge: Clean out your closet or room today. Find something you don't use anymore and donate it to a local charity or the DI.

deacon.title: The Guard of the Gate
deacon.message: I had rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God, than to dwell in the tents of wickedness. Deacons often act as 'ushers.' This is a holy guard duty.
deacon.challenge: The next time you are at church, be an 'active greeter.' Look people in the eye and give them a sincere smile as they enter the chapel.

deacon.title: The Sunday Pattern
deacon.message: That thou mayest more fully keep thyself unspotted from the world, thou shalt go to the house of prayer. The Sabbath is your 'refueling station.'
deacon.challenge: Identify the 'spots' (bad habits or thoughts) you picked up this week. In your heart, ask the Lord to wash them away as you participate in the sacrament.

deacon.title: Sunday Reflection: The Key-Holder
deacon.message: Reflection: How did you see the 'ministering of angels' this week? Was it a person, a thought, or a feeling?
deacon.challenge: Write your reflection in your journal.

deacon.title: The Power of the Quorum Presidency
deacon.message: A Deacon's President is given keys by the Stake President. These keys are real. They allow the President to receive revelation for YOU.
deacon.challenge: Ask your Quorum President today: 'Is there anyone in our quorum you're worried about? How can I help?'

deacon.title: Clean Hands and the Sacrament
deacon.message: Because you physically handle the bread and water, your physical 'cleanliness' (personal purity) represents your spiritual state.
deacon.challenge: Take a 10-minute walk today without any technology. Focus on keeping your thoughts 'clean' and 'virtuous' for the entire walk.

deacon.title: Small and Simple Things
deacon.message: Great things are brought to pass by small things. A Deacon who does his job well makes it possible for the whole ward to renew their covenants.
deacon.challenge: Do a 'small thing' for your Bishop today—send him a short text or email thanking him for his service.

deacon.title: Preparation for the Teachers Office
deacon.message: The Aaronic Priesthood is 'preparatory.' You are learning how to 'watch' over the church so you can one day be a Teacher.
deacon.challenge: Observe your Teachers today. What do they do differently than Deacons? What is one skill you want to learn from them?

deacon.title: The Power of the Priesthood in the Home
deacon.message: You have the authority to invite the Spirit into your home. When things get loud or angry, your 'standing ministry' can change the temperature.
deacon.challenge: If an argument starts at home today, don't join in. Be the one who uses a 'soft answer' to turn away wrath.

deacon.title: The Gift of the Holy Ghost
deacon.message: Angels speak by the power of the Holy Ghost. To hold the keys of the ministering of angels, you must be 'in tune' with the Ghost.
deacon.challenge: Pay attention to your first 'gut feeling' today. If it's a good thought, act on it immediately without second-guessing.

deacon.title: Sunday Reflection: The Prepared Soul
deacon.message: Reflection: Did you feel more 'prepared' to serve this Sunday than you did on Day 1?
deacon.challenge: Write your reflection in your journal.

deacon.title: The Duty of the Lesser Priesthood
deacon.message: The Deacon’s duty is to 'assist' the other offices. You are part of a massive team. There is no job 'too small' for a servant of God.
deacon.challenge: Identify a leader in your ward (Primary, Sunday School, or Young Women). Ask them: 'Is there anything I can help move or set up?'

deacon.title: Strength to Resist
deacon.message: The 'iron rod' is the word of God. A Deacon who knows his scriptures cannot be easily pulled off the path by friends or social media.
deacon.challenge: Pick one 'Hero' from the scriptures (like Nephi or Helaman). Read three chapters about them today and try to act like them.

deacon.title: The Sacredness of the Name
deacon.message: The name of the Lord is sacred. As a Priesthood holder, you represent that name. How you use His name in speech matters.
deacon.challenge: Listen to those around you today. If someone uses the Lord's name in vain, simply don't join in. Keep your own speech holy.

deacon.title: Preparation for the Temple
deacon.message: The Temple is the 'House of the Lord.' Your worthiness as a Deacon allows you to go there and perform baptisms for the dead.
deacon.challenge: Look at a picture of the Temple today. Remind yourself: 'I am worthy to enter that house because I hold the Priesthood.'

deacon.title: The Spirit of Elijah
deacon.message: Turning the hearts of the children to the fathers. Deacons are powerful family historians because they are fast with technology!
deacon.challenge: Open the 'FamilySearch' app. Find one person in your tree and look at their 'Memories.' Read one story out loud to a parent.

deacon.title: The Ordinance of the Bread
deacon.message: Jesus was the first to administer the sacrament. When you pass it, you are repeating the exact pattern He started 2,000 years ago.
deacon.challenge: Think about the word 'Remember.' During the sacrament this week, try to think only of Jesus and nothing else for those 10 minutes.

deacon.title: Sunday Reflection: The Steward
deacon.message: Reflection: What is the 'least' thing you did this week that actually felt 'much' (important) to God?
deacon.challenge: Write your reflection in your journal.

deacon.title: Priesthood is Service
deacon.message: Whosoever will be great among you, let him be your minister. Priesthood is not about being 'important'; it’s about being 'useful.'
deacon.challenge: Do one job today that no one else wants to do (like cleaning a bathroom or picking up trash). Do it for the Lord.

deacon.title: The Shield of Faith
deacon.message: Above all, taking the shield of faith, wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked. Your priesthood is your shield.
deacon.challenge: If a friend tries to get you to look at something or do something you know is wrong, 'lift your shield' and just say 'No thanks.'

deacon.title: The Power of Example
deacon.message: Let no man despise thy youth. You are young, but you are a Priesthood holder. That makes you a leader of other youth.
deacon.challenge: At school or out with friends today, be the one who suggests the 'good' activity or says the 'kind' word first.

deacon.title: Preparation for Mission
deacon.message: Serve him with all your heart, might, mind, and strength. You are 1/3 of the way through your training to be a full-time missionary.
deacon.challenge: Practice 'Preach My Gospel' today. Explain to a parent in 2 minutes: 'What is the Priesthood?'

deacon.title: Month 3 Mastery Reflection
deacon.message: Reflection: You have completed 3 months. How has your relationship with the 'ministering of angels' changed?
deacon.challenge: Share one experience from this month with your Quorum Advisor or Dad.

teacher.title: The Power of Presence
teacher.message: A Teacher’s duty is to 'be with and strengthen them.' Power in this office comes not from a distance, but from being present. Your physical presence in a home or meeting carries spiritual weight.
teacher.challenge: Identify a friend or family member who seems 'lonely' even when people are around. Spend 15 minutes of dedicated, distraction-free time just being with them today.

teacher.title: The Watchman’s Warning
teacher.message: The Lord uses the term 'Watchman' for those called to warn the people. As a Teacher, you are trained to see spiritual dangers before they arrive in the homes of the Saints.
teacher.challenge: Read Ezekiel 33:1–9. Identify one 'modern-day wolf' (like a specific media trend or habit) that you feel a duty to stay away from to protect your own spirit.

teacher.title: The Power of Persuasion
teacher.message: A Teacher 'warns, expounds, and exhorts.' This is done through persuasion, not force. Priesthood power only flows when you lead with love and 'pure knowledge.'
teacher.challenge: In a conversation today where you disagree with someone, try to persuade them using only 'gentleness' and 'meekness' rather than trying to 'win' the argument.

teacher.title: The Teacher’s Shield
teacher.message: To protect the Church, a Teacher must first be protected. Your 'shield of faith' quenches the fiery darts, allowing you to stand firm while others might waver.
teacher.challenge: Write down the 'fiery dart' (temptation) that hit you hardest this week. Pray specifically for a 'stronger shield' in that specific area tonight.

teacher.title: Strengthening the Feeble Knees
teacher.message: Part of 'strengthening the brethren' is noticing who is tired. A Teacher looks for those whose 'hands hang down' and offers a lift.
teacher.challenge: Notice who is doing a 'thankless' job today (a parent, a janitor, or a leader). Offer a sincere word of thanks to 'lift their hands' for a moment.

teacher.title: The Power of the Word
teacher.message: The word of God has a 'more powerful effect' than the sword. As a Teacher, your primary tool is the scripture. When you speak the word, hearts change.
teacher.challenge: Memorize one verse from the Book of Mormon today. Use it as your 'defense' if a negative thought enters your mind.

teacher.title: No Iniquity in the Church
teacher.message: Teachers see that 'there is no iniquity' or 'hardness' with each other. This starts with you. If you hold a grudge, the power of your office is blocked.
teacher.challenge: Is there someone you are 'hard' toward? Forgive them in your heart today, even if they haven't asked for it.

teacher.title: The Power of Invitation
teacher.message: A Teacher invites all to 'come unto Christ.' An invitation is a spiritual bridge. You aren't forcing; you are opening a door.
teacher.challenge: Invite a friend or sibling to do something 'wholesome' with you today—a walk, a game, or a service project.

teacher.title: Standing as a Witness
teacher.message: A Watchman stands as a witness 'at all times and in all things.' Your behavior at school or work is your most powerful 'teaching' moment.
teacher.challenge: In a group setting today, be the one who refuses to participate in gossip. Your silence will be a witness.

teacher.title: The Sabbath Guard
teacher.message: The Sabbath is a 'holy day.' A Teacher helps guard the sanctity of this day in their own home, setting the tone for reverence.
teacher.challenge: Prepare everything you need for Sunday (clothes, lessons, etc.) TODAY, so your Saturday night and Sunday morning are peaceful.

teacher.title: Sunday Reflection: The Strengthener
teacher.message: Reflection: 'When thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.' How has your own conversion grown this week as you’ve tried to strengthen others?
teacher.challenge: Write your reflection in your journal.

teacher.title: The Power of the Quorum Council
teacher.message: The Teacher's Quorum President presides over 24 teachers. In a council, there is safety and power. You are not a 'lone watchman.'
teacher.challenge: Text a member of your quorum today just to say: 'I’m glad you’re in our quorum.' Unity is power.

teacher.title: The Gift of Discernment
teacher.message: Discernment is the 'Watchman’s Gift.' It is the ability to see things as they really are. A Teacher prays for this gift to know how to help his families.
teacher.challenge: Before you interact with your family tonight, pray: 'Lord, help me see what they are feeling but not saying.'

teacher.title: The Law of the Gospel
teacher.message: Teachers shall 'teach the principles of my gospel.' You don't need to be an expert in everything, just the core principles of faith and repentance.
teacher.challenge: Explain the 'Plan of Salvation' to a stuffed animal or an empty chair in 3 minutes. Practice makes your 'teaching' power natural.

teacher.title: Preparation for the Priest’s Office
teacher.message: The Priest's duty includes 'baptizing' and 'administering the sacrament.' You are preparing for these sacred 'saving' ordinances by first learning to 'watch' over the people.
teacher.challenge: Watch the Priests during the sacrament this Sunday. Observe the specific prayers they say. Imagine yourself saying those words soon.

teacher.title: The Power of Virtue
teacher.message: Let virtue garnish thy thoughts unceasingly; then shall thy confidence wax strong in the presence of God. A Teacher with a clean mind has 'confidence' that others lack.
teacher.challenge: If a tempting image or thought appears today, replace it immediately with a 'virtuous' thought (like a favorite scripture or memory).

teacher.title: The Spirit of Truth
teacher.message: He that preacheth by the Spirit of truth receiveth it as it is preached. When you share a truth, the Spirit teaches BOTH you and the listener.
teacher.challenge: Share one spiritual 'truth' you believe with a parent or friend today. Notice how YOU feel as you say it.

teacher.title: Sunday Reflection: The Watchman
teacher.message: Reflection: 'I have set watchmen upon thy walls.' How did you 'stand on the wall' for your ward or family this week?
teacher.challenge: Write your reflection in your journal.

teacher.title: The Power of Example
teacher.message: Be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity. This is the Teacher’s primary lesson plan.
teacher.challenge: Pick one of those six areas (word, conversation, charity, spirit, faith, or purity) and focus on being a 'perfect example' of it for 24 hours.

teacher.title: The Armor of Light
teacher.message: Let us cast off the works of darkness, and let us put on the armor of light. A Teacher carries a light that dispels the darkness in a home.
teacher.challenge: Is there a 'dark' corner of your life (a secret habit or a lie)? Cast it off today by talking to your Bishop or a parent. Put on the light.

teacher.title: The Power of Sincerity
teacher.message: Enos prayed with 'mighty prayer and supplication.' A Teacher who prays sincerely for his families will receive specific ideas on how to help them.
teacher.challenge: Choose one family you minister to. Pray for them by name, and ask for ONE thing you can do this week to make their life easier.

teacher.title: The Keeper of the Gate
teacher.message: The keeper of the gate is the Holy One of Israel. As a Teacher, you help lead people to that gate. You are a 'gate-opener' for others.
teacher.challenge: Who do you know that feels 'shut out' or 'unwelcome' at church? Reach out to them today and let them know they are wanted.

teacher.title: The Strength of the Quorum
teacher.message: A threefold cord is not quickly broken. When Teachers stand together, they are unbreakable. Your quorum is your 'squad' for spiritual battle.
teacher.challenge: Find a way to serve WITH another quorum member today. Even a 10-minute joint project builds that 'threefold cord.'

teacher.title: The Teacher’s Reward
teacher.message: They become the sons of Moses and of Aaron and the seed of Abraham. Your service as a Teacher connects you to the greatest men who ever lived.
teacher.challenge: Read about one 'Teacher' from church history (like a young Joseph Smith or a faithful home teacher). What inspired you about them?

teacher.title: Sunday Reflection: The Sentinel
teacher.message: Reflection: 'I will stand upon my watch, and set me upon the tower.' What did you see from your 'tower' this week?
teacher.challenge: Write your reflection in your journal.

teacher.title: Teaching with Authority
teacher.message: Jesus taught as 'one having authority, and not as the scribes.' Priesthood authority is the right to speak for God. Use it with reverence.
teacher.challenge: When you share a spiritual thought today, don't say 'I think...' or 'Maybe...' Say 'I know...' or 'The Lord has promised...'

teacher.title: The Power of Forgiveness
teacher.message: The Lord requires us to forgive all men. A Teacher who carries bitterness cannot 'strengthen' anyone. Forgiveness is a power-release.
teacher.challenge: Is there a past 'hurt' you are still nursing? Let it go today. Tell the Lord in prayer: 'I am leaving this with You.'

teacher.title: The Watchman’s Courage
teacher.message: Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid. Sometimes being a Teacher means standing alone in your standards. The Lord is with you.
